dedupe_keys.name: neteventsimulator mobile network events micro simulator

description: NetEventSimulator is a C++ framework for micro-simulation of mobile network data, written by Bogdan Oancea for the European Statistical System's ESSnet Big Data work on mobile phone data for official statistics. It moves a synthetic population with mobile devices across a map and generates the network events their phones would produce at a configured set of antennas, while keeping the true positions as a latent ground truth that real network data never provide. Inputs are a WKT map, a simulation file (grid, population size, length, mobility parameters), an antenna file with operators, power, path-loss exponent and azimuth and elevation patterns, a population file with device ownership, and optional prior probabilities for device-location estimation. Seven sample input sets are included. Coverage: any area a user draws; not tied to a country. Format and access: source on GitHub under the EUPL-1.2 licence, archived on Zenodo (version 1.3.1, May 2026); builds on Windows, Linux and macOS with the GEOS library. Caveats: synthetic data with simplified radio and mobility models; code revisions may occur without notice. Simulation uses: testing methods that turn network events into population presence and flows, agent-based mobility of people with phones, and planning scenarios where antennas fail. Related records: the Italian mobile network metadata population dataset and the Telecom Italia Big Data Challenge are real-data counterparts.
